result.topic_en: The page sketches a proof, using Minkowski's theorem, that a function of n variables admitting infinitely many integral linear transformations into itself is an ordinary or simultaneous semi-invariant, and then begins listing properties of invariants.

items.english: If a function of n variables admits infinitely many linear transformations with integer coefficients into itself, then, as one can prove with Minkowski's theorem, there is at least one substitution of infinitely high order which leaves the function unchanged.

items.english: If one brings this substitution to its canonical form, one recognizes that the function is an ordinary or simultaneous semi-invariant.
